12Proof-Carrying Numbers (PCN): A Protocol for Trustworthy Numeric Answers from LLMs via Claim Verification

Solatorio, 2025. Snapshot captured 2026-07-31. In the store as citation:pcn2025: 7/7 claims verified, 6 fields of evidence.

the output

Proof-Carrying Numbers emits claim-bound tokens tied to structured claims, places verification in the renderer, not the model under declared policies such as exact equality, rounding, aliases, or tolerance, and its published description does not cover entity scoping or a named vocabulary for qualitative judgments. The checks are deterministic: Under PCN, a number is marked as “verified” only if it is bound to an authoritative claim and passes deterministic checks at the presentation layer. Its own scope statement: PCN secures numeric fidelity only.

13Towards Verifiable Text Generation with Symbolic References

Torroba Hennigen et al., 2024. Snapshot captured 2026-07-31. In the store as citation:symgen: 10/10 claims verified, 9 fields of evidence.

the output

SymGen has the model interleave its regular output text with explicit symbolic references to fields present in some conditioning data, so a wrong number is impossible and so is reporting one; in its human study the annotations were reducing the average verification time by 20%, and in its method A parser then substitutes the symbolic references with their corresponding values in the structured data (e.g., Portland for visitor . city ) to obtain the final rendered text (3).. Its limitations section concedes: Although it is capable of generating accurate symbolic references, the surrounding context text may still be incorrect, thus leading to verifiable but incorrect generations. And symbolic references may be incorrect even when the final text is accurate; for example if two fields in our data have the same value, but a symbolic reference is made to the wrong field, then the rendered text would be correct but not the reference. The check it offers is a person's: The references can be used to display the provenance of different spans of text in the generation, reducing the effort required for manual verification. And Our SymGen pipeline can implicitly leverage the input data to generate prose without any symbolic references. It is offered as a simple approach for enabling easier manual validation of an LLM’s output. Automatic verification it places outside itself: LLM verification is an orthogonal improvement to the reliability of LLMs, where the output of an LLM is automatically verified.
